title: Removable media, availability and observed performance
summary: USB/removable drives are normal providers. Their stable provider/volume identity is independent of the current mount path; catalogue knowledge survives disconnection. Availability and performance are separate observations.
invariants: An offline removable replica remains in the catalogue with OFFLINE state.
A removable provider offers workspace only while connected and admitted.
Performance is measured/observed rather than inferred from labels such as USB or cloud.
Intermittent availability is not equivalent to poor throughput; a connected USB hard disk may be preferable to a slow remote provider.
Planner logic may prefer waiting for a known fast removable provider over beginning a very slow remote materialisation when policy permits.

provenance.claim: Regression proves stable removable-provider identity, offline catalogue continuity and observed performance semantics.
